text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.6% today to $136.27, continuing a sharp two-week decline of nearly 10% that accelerated after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th. The stock has lost $18 per share since late October, suggesting investors reacted negatively to the earnings results or guidance—though the specific details aren't clear from the data provided. Oil prices remain relatively stable (US crude at $99.64/barrel, global at $107), so the selloff appears tied to the company's own performance rather than a broader energy market collapse.

The broader political backdrop may also be weighing on the sector. The midterm elections delivered a decisive rejection of Trump-era policies, including strong momentum behind renewable energy expansion. For an oil and gas producer like ConocoPhillips, this signals potential headwinds from stricter climate policies and accelerated competition from clean energy—a longer-term concern that could be dampening investor appetite even as crude prices hold steady.
